name: Gary Josephson
bio: Gary Josephson is an independent candidate for Ohio's 15th Congressional District in 2026. He attended The Ohio State University and was the Democratic nominee for the same seat in 2022, losing the general election.

platform.point: Supports universal health care.
Says coal is in the past and favors sustainable energy and sustainable agriculture.
Backs green-job creation through public-private partnerships.
Proposes letting borrowers work off student debt through community service.
Wants to remove obstacles that keep people from voting.

welfare.evidence: Has called for universal health care.

liberty.evidence: Supports reproductive rights (abortion) and a right to self-defense while opposing unlimited access to firepower (guns).

energy.evidence: Says coal's time has passed and backs sustainable energy and green jobs.

notes: Platform and scores come from his 2022 campaign as a Democrat, as shown on BallotReady; 2026 statements as an independent could not be verified. His campaign site and Ballotpedia could not be loaded, and social handles are as listed by BallotReady.

name: Mark Tedford
bio: Mark Tedford has represented District 69 (Jenks and south Tulsa) in the Oklahoma House of Representatives since 2022. He is an insurance agent and Tulsa-area businessman who grew up in Jenks. He holds degrees from Missouri Southern State University, the University of Tulsa and Biola University.

platform.point: Aims to lower family costs by cutting inflationary spending and regulation and restoring fiscal discipline.
Calls for strict border enforcement and putting American citizens and workers first.
Pledges to eliminate wasteful federal spending, fraud and abuse and strengthen accountability.
Wants to expand American energy production and support manufacturing, skilled trades and domestic hiring.
Promises to protect constitutional rights, parental rights and religious liberty.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on cutting spending and regulatory red tape.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to protect the unborn (abortion, community norms) and defend the Second Amendment (guns, individual choice).

immigration.evidence: Calls for strict enforcement of immigration law and border security.

energy.evidence: Pledges to unleash American energy production.

education.evidence: Backs parental rights, while in the legislature he has advocated higher teacher pay.

faith.evidence: Lists defending faith and religious liberty among his top priorities.

notes: The Commons portrait (File:Tedford Mark OKHouse.jpg) is marked public domain by the Oklahoma Legislative Service Bureau without a specific free licence or statute, so it was not used.

name: John Croisant
current_role: Member of the Tulsa Public Schools Board
bio: John Croisant is a member of the Tulsa Public Schools Board. He describes himself as a fifth-generation small-business owner based in Tulsa.

platform.point: Supports broader coverage through Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies or universal coverage, and opposes recent federal Medicaid cuts.
Wants stronger public schools, more special-education support and a debt-free teacher education program tied to public-school service.
Backs term limits, overturning Citizens United, banning stock trading by officials and Supreme Court ethics rules.
Supports secure borders plus a path to citizenship for long-term taxpaying residents, shifting ICE resources to court backlogs.
Calls for federal AI rules protecting workers and young people and treats addictive algorithms as a public-health issue.
Wants HUD focused on building affordable housing and treats childcare access as an economic investment.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies or universal coverage and expanded childcare access.

security.evidence: Backs smart law-enforcement resourcing and cybersecurity investment while opposing use of government power against political opponents.

immigration.evidence: Pairs border security and accountability with a path to citizenship for long-term residents.

foreign.evidence: Favors redirecting defense spending to domestic needs rather than ongoing military involvement abroad.

energy.evidence: Supports a diversified mix including oil and gas while shifting toward renewable sources.

tech.evidence: Calls for federal AI legislation and opposes addictive algorithms and media monopolies.

education.evidence: Supports public schools and opposes unrestricted private-school subsidies.

faith.evidence: Supports church-state separation and opposes religious instruction in public schools.

notes: The campaign lists its social accounts only through a Linktree page, so no individual accounts were recorded. An earlier liberty score was removed because his issues page does not address guns, abortion or drugs.

name: Josh Brecheen
bio: Josh Brecheen has represented Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District since 2023 and is a member of the Freedom Caucus. He served in the Oklahoma Senate from 2010 to 2018 and earlier worked as a field representative for U.S. Senator Tom Coburn. Born in Ada, he is a Choctaw Nation citizen and Oklahoma State University graduate who has run speaking and trucking businesses.

platform.point: Wants the border closed to all but legal immigration, framing it as a national-security issue.
Seeks deep federal budget cuts to fight inflation and the national debt.
Supports term limits for members of Congress and pledges to follow them himself.
Holds that life begins at conception and opposes abortion.
Opposes a federal role in education, calling it a parental responsibility.
Opposes defunding police and backs law enforcement and gun rights.

economy.evidence: Calls for large federal spending cuts to reduce inflation and debt.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion, introduced a bill to bar federal funds for Pride events (LGBTQ) and strongly supports gun rights.

security.evidence: Opposes defunding police and prioritizes law enforcement and national defense.

immigration.evidence: Wants the border closed except for legal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Voted against the 2024 Ukraine aid package and to withdraw troops from Syria, while backing Israel.

education.evidence: Says education belongs to parents and opposes federal involvement.

faith.evidence: Grounds his abortion stance in faith and as a state senator filed bills encouraging creation-evolution debate in schools.

notes: An earlier energy score was removed because neither his campaign issues page nor Wikipedia states an energy position.

name: Brandon Wade
bio: Brandon Wade is a machinery assembler and union member from Oklahoma. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2022 and was the Democratic nominee for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District in 2024.

platform.point: Wants wealthy individuals and corporations to pay more, with a 21-28% corporate rate, and replacing harmful tariffs.
Seeks to separate health coverage from employment through Medicare for All, regulated insurance or a hybrid.
Proposes lifting the Social Security payroll tax cap to raise benefits and extend solvency.
Supports writing Roe v. Wade protections into federal law.
Backs more border agents and immigration judges plus streamlined paths to citizenship.
Wants to protect public-school funding and keep the Department of Education.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations.

welfare.evidence: Supports decoupling health care from jobs, including Medicare for All, and expanding Social Security.

liberty.evidence: Supports codifying Roe (abortion) and LGBTQ+ protections.

security.evidence: Backs modern border surveillance while calling for transparent enforcement and due process.

immigration.evidence: Proposes faster immigration courts, work authorization for pending cases and streamlined citizenship.

education.evidence: Wants public-school funding protected and opposes dismantling the Education Department.

notes: Occupation comes from Wikipedia's election page.

name: Ronnie Hopkins
bio: Ronnie Hopkins is a pastor from eastern Oklahoma. He ran as an independent for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District in 2024, receiving about 4% of the vote.

platform.point: Proposes turning Social Security into personal trust accounts that allow retirement at 60 and can be left to heirs.
Wants to reduce foreign aid.
Pledges support for veterans.
Supports Second Amendment rights.
Says running without a party frees him from party control and lobbyists.

welfare.evidence: Proposes converting Social Security into individually owned trust accounts.

liberty.evidence: Supports gun rights and opposes government overreach into personal choices (guns).

faith.evidence: Emphasizes biblical principles as a basis for his campaign.

notes: All positions come from his 2024 campaign; no 2026-specific statements were found. His campaign site appears to date from 2024.

name: Frank Lucas
bio: Frank Lucas has served in the U.S. House since a 1994 special election, representing Oklahoma's 3rd District since 2003. He chaired the House Agriculture Committee (2011-2015) and the Science, Space and Technology Committee (2023-2025), and earlier served in the Oklahoma House. A farmer and rancher from Cheyenne, he graduated from Oklahoma State University.

platform.point: Supports family farms, rural broadband, rural hospitals and fair trade.
Favors tax cuts, deregulation and free trade.
Backs border security funding and reforms favoring skilled workers and simpler farm-worker programs.
Supports robust military funding, including Oklahoma's Altus and Vance Air Force bases.
Supports Second Amendment rights and anti-abortion legislation.
Commits to accessible health care and education benefits for veterans.

liberty.evidence: Backs anti-abortion legislation and gun rights.

immigration.evidence: Supports border security funding alongside skilled and agricultural worker programs.

foreign.evidence: Supports strong military funding and belongs to the Congressional Taiwan Caucus.

tech.evidence: Voted for the Merger Filing Fee Modernization Act of 2022 antitrust package.

name: Suzie Byrd
bio: Suzie Byrd, of Enid, won the Democratic nomination for Oklahoma's 3rd Congressional District in June 2026. Raised in Hennessey and an Oklahoma State University graduate, she most recently worked as a reporter for the Enid News & Eagle and has owned or partnered in businesses in Oklahoma and Florida.
notes: News summaries say her Facebook page prioritizes universal health care, affordable housing, immigration reform and education reform, but this could not be checked directly. No campaign website was found.

name: Tom Cole
bio: Tom Cole has represented Oklahoma's 4th District since 2003 and has chaired the House Appropriations Committee since 2024. He previously served in the Oklahoma Senate, as Oklahoma Secretary of State and as chair of the NRCC. A Chickasaw Nation citizen, he holds a PhD in British history from the University of Oklahoma.

platform.point: Calls securing the border and stopping illegal immigration a top priority.
Advocates balancing the budget and reforming entitlements to reduce debt.
Supports a strong, well-equipped military to meet modern threats.
Backs an all-of-the-above strategy with more domestic production and alternative energy.
Works to limit unneeded regulation on farmers while keeping safety nets like crop insurance.
Supports legal protection for the unborn.

economy.evidence: Advocates balancing the budget and reforming entitlements.

welfare.evidence: Opposes the Affordable Care Act and calls for entitlement reform.

liberty.evidence: Consistently votes against abortion and for gun rights.

immigration.evidence: Calls border security and stopping illegal immigration a top priority.

foreign.evidence: Champions a strong national defense and voted to support Israel after October 7.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above strategy emphasizing domestic production.

tech.evidence: Voted for the Merger Filing Fee Modernization Act of 2022 antitrust package.

name: Mitchell Jacob
bio: Mitchell Jacob is a public defender and fourth-generation Oklahoman from Tulsa. He served 5.5 years in the U.S. Army as a cryptologic linguist, deploying to Syria, and earlier worked in mortgage, banking and brokerage jobs. He earned a law degree from the University of Oklahoma in 2025.

platform.point: Calls the debt a major threat and wants to stop raising the debt limit and cut spending.
Supports fully funding public schools, free school meals and improving reading proficiency.
Wants faster processing of visas and asylum claims and opposes the large enforcement budget and ICE.
Treats health care as a right and wants affordable care without insurance denials.
Favors rehabilitation, opposes for-profit prisons and wants to reduce recidivism.
Proposes the HOPE Act targeting illegal gun transfers to minors and negligent storage.

economy.evidence: Wants spending cuts and debt reduction while criticizing tariffs' effect on consumer prices.

welfare.evidence: Calls health care a human right and backs free school meals.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights while proposing targeted gun rules focused on minors and storage (abortion, guns).

security.evidence: Favors rehabilitation, body cameras and ICE transparency, and calls for abolishing ICE.

immigration.evidence: Opposes mass-deportation tactics and the enforcement budget and supports faster legal processing.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending U.S. economic, political and military support for Israel until the bombing stops.

tech.evidence: Supports thoughtful AI regulation covering worker, environmental and child-safety effects.

notes: His campaign says the administration's birthright-citizenship order prompted him to switch from a state House bid to this race.

name: Rocco Bonacci
current_role: Disability advocate; member of the Lawton Access Board
bio: Rocco Bonacci, of Lawton, is a disability advocate and member of the Lawton Access Board. He is a retired U.S. Air Force fighter pilot who commanded Air Force Basic Military Training in San Antonio before settling in Oklahoma.
notes: Background comes from KOSU's candidate list as summarised in search results; no campaign website or policy statements were found.

name: Stephanie Bice
bio: Stephanie Bice has represented Oklahoma's 5th District since 2021 and serves on the Appropriations and House Administration committees. She served in the Oklahoma Senate from 2014 to 2020 and earlier worked in finance and business development in the technology and marketing sectors. Born in Oklahoma City, she is an Oklahoma State University graduate.

platform.point: Pushes to expand veterans' access to health care, job training and education benefits.
Supports stronger immigration enforcement and redirected unused funds to the National Guard.
Introduced legislation to eliminate duplicative federal grant programs.
Supports Oklahoma oil and gas and opposes regulations she sees as threatening production.
Leads bipartisan efforts to expand paid family leave through small-business tax credits.
Backs protections for free speech, religious liberty, due process and gun rights.

economy.evidence: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and seeks federal spending cuts.

liberty.evidence: Defends Second Amendment rights and free speech (guns, speech); her campaign issues page does not address abortion.

immigration.evidence: Supports stronger immigration enforcement and border security.

foreign.evidence: Backed Israel military aid after October 2023 and voted against a 2026 Iran war powers resolution.

energy.evidence: Supports the oil and gas industry and opposes regulations on domestic production.

faith.evidence: Lists protecting religious liberty among her constitutional priorities.

notes: An unverified education score was removed; the liberty score was lowered because only gun and speech positions could be confirmed.
